name: Vertical Strike Arbitrage
summary: A vertical spread quoted for a credit larger than the strike width, or a debit spread quoted at zero or negative cost, violates option monotonicity and is riskless profit if the quotes are real.

legs.strike_rule: Higher strike K2 = K1 + width, where the observed credit for selling this spread exceeds (K2 - K1) x 100, or the debit for buying it is <= 0

max_profit: credit_received - (width x 100) when the credit exceeds the width, or simply (width x 100) when a debit spread was bought for nothing
max_loss: Zero if the quotes are real and both legs fill. In reality: the fees and the slippage from a fill that does not occur at the displayed price.

greeks.delta: small and irrelevant — the trade is a pricing violation, not an exposure

breakevens: None — profit at every terminal price if the violation was real.
when_to_use: As a continuous scan on the option chain. Any credit call spread where credit > width, or any debit call spread where debit <= 0, is either an arbitrage or a data error. In 2026 on liquid names it is always a data error, a locked/crossed market, or a stale leg.
entry_rules: LEVEL 3 LEGAL: a vertical spread is fully covered within the same multi-leg order, so Alpaca accepts it. This is one of the few genuinely executable arbitrage patterns in the family.

MANDATORY: submit as a SINGLE multi-leg order with a limit price. Never leg it — the violation exists for milliseconds and a half-filled spread is a naked short option, which Level 3 will reject on the second leg and which leaves an unintended exposure.
Scan gate: for a call vertical, flag when (K1_call_bid - K2_call_ask) x 100 > (K2 - K1) x 100 + fees + $10. For a put vertical, the symmetric test.
Pre-trade checks: both legs' quotes timestamped within 2 seconds, displayed size >= 10 on both, underlying not halted, no OCC contract adjustment on either strike, same expiry and same deliverable.
Both strikes must have OI >= 100. A violation involving a zero-OI strike is a phantom.
Do not chase: one limit order at the arbitrage price, cancel after 3 seconds if unfilled.
management_rules: Nothing to manage if the violation was real — the position is worth at least zero at every price.
If only part of the intended size fills, accept the partial and do not increase the limit price.
If the spread was established at a genuine arbitrage price, it can simply be held to expiry — but the assignment guard below still applies, because the short leg is American and share-settled.
exit_rules: MANDATORY ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short leg no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally, even though it is covered by the long leg. Assignment would deliver 100 shares and force an exercise of the long leg to unwind, with settlement-timing exposure in between.
If the short leg goes ITM with extrinsic below $0.05 at any time, close the whole spread that session.
Close the short call by 15:00 ET the session before any ex-dividend date if its extrinsic value is below 1.25 x the declared dividend.
If both legs finish ITM, close the spread rather than allowing the offsetting exercise and assignment to settle.
assignment_risk: On the short leg, and it is fully covered by the long leg in payoff terms, so there is no unbounded exposure. But covered is not the same as harmless for a never-be-assigned system: assignment creates a 100-share position that must be unwound by exercising the long leg, which takes a session and carries the shares overnight.
buying_power: For a credit vertical: (width x 100) - credit received. If the credit exceeds the width, the net requirement is effectively zero or negative, which is itself a red flag worth checking against broker margin logic before assuming it.
liquidity_needs: Both strikes need real displayed size. Violations concentrated in zero-volume strikes are quote artefacts.
common_mistakes: Legging in. Acting on midpoint-derived 'violations' rather than executable bid/ask. Not checking for adjusted contracts, where a violation against unadjusted assumptions is normal and correct.
zero_dte_notes: Apparent violations spike at 0DTE near the close when market makers widen. Almost all are stale. If one is taken, the 15:40 ET short-leg close rule becomes the same-minute close rule.
